text: How do noise cancelling headphones work? It's very physics-y. So it's very engineering-y. There are microphones on the outside or inside of the headphones. Some headphones are called feedforward. They have the microphone on the outside and they pick up the noise before it reaches your ear. Some headphones are called feedback, they pick up the noise after it reached the ear, closer to the speaker. And then the digital signal processor analyzes the waveform and reconstructs it in real time. It gets the frequency, amplitude, phase. And then it creates the anti-noise. The exact same sound, but inverted, opposite phase. So when the noise meets the anti-noise, it will cancel out, because the peaks will meet the troughs and cancel out. And that's very good for low frequency, constant noise, like airplane engine noise, air conditioning noise, road noise. And not so good for higher frequency, more transient noises. Like a baby crying or a door slamming. Those are more difficult to cancel. And also, you still have some passive noise isolation from the ear pads themselves. And they cancel a bit more higher frequency noise. And then you have hybrid noise cancellation that combines both. So it's just picking up noise, inverting it, adding it back to cancel out. So that helps with blocking out a lot of sound especially in high frequencies. So it's almost like wearing earplugs. But it doesn't really cancel low frequency sounds like the rumbling of airplane engines or of traffic. The other part is active noise cancellation, which basically uses little microphones outside or inside the headphones to sample the sound in the environment. And then it creates a mirror wave to the sound it hears. So the anti-noise wave is opposite of the noise wave. And then when they meet together, they cancel out each other. That's why it works really well for very constant sounds. It's more difficult to cancel out sound from say a person talking or a dog barking, because it's not very constant, it's very fast changing. But in most cases, especially modern headphones, you have both passive and active noise cancellation. So passive handles high frequency noise. Active handles the low frequency noise. And then you have transparency mode, where you actually want to hear the noise outside. And that's also using the mic, and then adaptive noise cancellation. Which will adjust the noise cancellation depending on the environment that you're in. So you don't really get silence, but it's a lot quieter. You can play the music at lower volumes. You're less tired, and it works really well in noisy environments. It cancels most of the noise, but not all of it.
